issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising second-appellate or civil-revisional jurisdiction may interfere with a factual finding when the finding lacks legal evidence, rests on a misreading of evidence, has a materially prejudicial legal infirmity, or is perverse.
material_facts: The lower courts found that the disputed property was within the area claimed to have been notified as a slum area.

The High Court found that the tenants had not proved the disputed property's identity with the area covered by the notification; the documents relied on did not identify the suit property, and the supporting oral evidence was insufficient.
The landlady disputed the property's identity and relied on evidence indicating that it was in a different survey area that had not been notified.
issues.conclusion: The High Court committed no error in reassessing the factual findings because the tenants had not established the factual basis for the protection they claimed with legal and cogent evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Factual findings ordinarily are not reversed in second appeal or civil revision. However, interference is permissible where a finding is without legal evidence, based on a misreading of evidence, affected by a legal infirmity that materially prejudices a party, or perverse. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: second_appeal_or_civil_revision and (finding_without_legal_evidence or finding_based_on_misread_evidence or materially_prejudicial_legal_infirmity or perverse_finding)

predicates.second_appeal_or_civil_revision: A party asks a High Court to review a factual finding in a second appeal or civil revision.
predicates.finding_without_legal_evidence: A lower court made the factual finding without legal evidence supporting it.
predicates.finding_based_on_misread_evidence: A lower court's factual finding rests on a misreading of the evidence.
predicates.materially_prejudicial_legal_infirmity: A legal infirmity in the factual finding materially prejudices a party's case.
predicates.perverse_finding: A lower court made a factual finding that is perverse.

issues.definition: When a High Court is reviewing a factual finding in a second appeal or civil revision, it may set the finding aside if at least one of the stated defects is present.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking relief based on statutory protection for occupants of a notified slum area must prove that the disputed property is within the area covered by the notification.
material_facts: The tenants brought suits seeking relief based on the claim that their property lay in a notified slum area and that eviction proceedings required prior permission.
The landlady denied that the property was in the survey area said to have been notified and presented evidence identifying it with a different survey area.
The documents relied on by the tenants did not identify the disputed property, and the High Court found their oral evidence insufficient to prove that it was within the notified area.
issues.conclusion: The burden was on the tenant-plaintiffs to establish the identity of the disputed property and prove that it lay in the notified slum area; because they failed to do so, they were not entitled to the injunction based on the statutory protection.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3 and 29 of the Tamil Nadu Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1971, the claimed protection depended on the property being in an area declared a slum area. A plaintiff seeking affirmative relief on that basis bears the burden of proving the facts that entitle the plaintiff to relief, including the property's identity and its location within the notified area. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.plaintiff_sought_relief_based_on_slum_ar: A plaintiff sought relief on the basis that statutory protection applied to occupants of a notified slum area.
predicates.plaintiff_claimed_property_was_in_notifi: The plaintiff claimed that the disputed property was within an area declared a slum area.
predicates.defendant_disputed_property_identity_or_: The defendant disputed that the property's identity or location placed it within the area covered by the notification.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks relief based on slum-area protection, claims the property is in the notified area, and the defendant disputes that claim, the plaintiff must prove that the property is in the notified area.
